There’s no significance to that. We want to be able to dig a little bit deeper into the culture, into the culinary culture, but also the culture of the city itself, or the place itself, or the people themselves.” “I think what this documentary allows us to do is to show people that you can be courageously vulnerable. articles.title: Sebastián Lelio Dies: Oscar-Winning ‘A Fantastic Woman’ Filmmaker Who Also Made ‘The Wonder’ & ‘The Wave’ Was 52
articles.content: Sebastián Lelio , the Oscar-winning Chilean writer-director behind such pics as A Fantastic Woman , The Wonder , and The Wave , died Friday in Santiago. He was 52. His family confirmed the news in a social media post from Lelio’s partner Amalia Kassai, and local media in Chile reported that he was found dead at his home. Kassai’s post said he died “following health complications” but did not provide an exact cause. “With great sadness, we announce the death, following health complications, of Chilean filmmaker Sebastián Lelio,” she wrote in a translation. “We are going through a time of profound grief, and his memory will remain with us forever. He was a wonderful person who made significant contributions to Chilean culture at important moments in its history. As a family, we ask for privacy and consideration during these difficult times.” Lelio had been filming Chilean Poet, an adaptation of Alejandro Zambra’s novel. He had another project, Voyagers starring Andrew Garfield as the astronomer Carl Sagan alongside Daisy Edgar-Jones as Cosmos filmmaker Ann Druyan, in the works. Several of Lelio’s films tell female-focused stories. His 2017 pic A Fantastic Woman won the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film , the only time Chile has won the category now called Best International Feature Film. It premiered at the Berlin Film Festival that year, winning three awards including Best Feature Film and Screenplay, and later won a Spirit Award and numerous other accolades. articles.title: Adam Driver Explains ‘X-Men’ Came Along At “Right Time” After Years Of Rejecting Marvel Roles: “All Kind Of Came Together”
articles.content: After years of rejected offers, Adam Driver is finally joining the MCU with Jake Schreier’s take on X-Men . The 2x Oscar nominee recently explained that the role of Nathaniel Millbury/Mister Sinister came along at what “felt like a right time,” following several attempts on Kevin Feige ‘s behalf to court the actor into joining the Marvel Studios fold. “I was a big X-Men fan when I was a kid,” he explained on Jimmy Kimmel Live . “Me and my cousin, Tony, he would be Sabretooth and I would be Wolverine. It’s a big deal.” Driver added, “I was a big fan. I mean, I was a fan of the other things too. But this one felt like a right time, and then it’s X-Men.” Watch on Deadline As Kimmel noted, Feige previously revealed his “ long-lived tradition ” of getting on a Zoom with Driver to offer him an MCU role, only for the actor to think about it and pass on the project a few days later. “It was really X-Men and Jake Schreier, who’s the director, his idea for it, and that it’s Kevin Feige,” explained Driver. “You know, it all kind of came together. The script is really cool.” Following his casting announcement at D23 in August, the pressure is on for Driver. “A lot of people are going to watch it, and if it’s bad, a lot of people will see you being bad. Plus, I do’’t want to mess it up. I’m a huge fan of X-Men,” he told Kimmel. Driver joins Christopher Abbott as Charles Xavier/Professor X, Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm, Kit Connor as Cyclops, Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Samara Weaving as Emma Frost and Asa Germann as Angel. Scheduled to premiere May 5, 2028 in theaters, Marvel tapped Schreier to direct X-Men last May after his previous MCU title Thunderbolts* premiered. Beef creator Lee Sung Jin and The Bear showrunner Joanna Calo are writing the script.

articles.content: As James Bond casting rumors heat up, a couple more A-list actors have entered the mix: Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult were among the stars who screen-tested to play the new 007. Both British actors certainly have the acting pedigree to play the suave spy, taking up the mantle after Daniel Craig’s 15-year run. They also have a keen awareness of what it takes to work in major franchise fare: Pattinson stars as Batman for DC Studios and is an alum of both the “Twilight” and “Harry Potter” franchises; meanwhile, Hoult plays Lex Luthor in DC’s Superman movies and starred in the 2010s “X-Men” prequel trilogy. He next stars in the Amazon MGM Studios movie “How to Rob a Bank,” in theaters on Nov. 13. Pattinson also has the Denis Villeneuve factor on his side, after starring in the filmmaker’s upcoming epic “Dune: Part Three.” Related Stories Apple Services Revenue Hits New Record of $31.6 Billion in September Quarter, but Growth Is Slowing Down Last year, Amazon MGM Studios tapped Villeneuve as the franchise’s next director, with “Peaky Blinders” creator Steven Knight hired to write the script. Getting Bond 26 off the ground has been a top priority for the property’s new stewards, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman. Since then, nearly every 30-something British actor’s name has been bandied about in the U.K. and U.S. press, with rumored top contenders including Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden. Variety has learned that Harry Styles has had discussions about the part, and Theo James, 41, also hasn’t been ruled out. Pierce Brosnan, the Bond of the ’90s, recently gave his stamp of approval to Turner, while Gary Oldman threw his weight behind Lowden, his “Slow Horses” co-star. (Oldman also claimed that the next James Bond has already been picked, but no official casting announcement has been made.)

articles.title: Cannes, Annecy-Winning ‘Iron Boy’ Producer Eddy Cinema Backs Memory-Erasure Animation ‘Wilderness of the Greenriver’ at Taiwan Creative Content Fest
articles.content: A man who has no memory of his past finds out that a patient is the sister he lost in “ Wilderness of the Greenriver ,” an animated feature from Barcelona-based Hong Kong director Ellis Kayin Chan that is at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest ( TCCF ) in Taipei. The film is set in a world where technology lets people wipe out painful memories. When Arin learns that a patient named Zia is his sister, the discovery shakes what he believes and unlocks memories of a childhood he had forgotten. He has to decide whether to uphold the system or embrace his own humanity. Related Stories Tristan Thompson Boards Jason Zada's Bitcoin Creator Movie 'Satoshi' as Producer (EXCLUSIVE) The story is rooted in Chan’s own loss. He says the film grew from a simple conviction: “Pain is not the enemy of being human – forgetting is.” “I grew up believing that if I stayed calm, if I didn’t feel too much, I could stay safe. When my sister and I grew apart, I tried to erase the pain connected to her. What I didn’t realize was that I was also erasing the tenderness, the care, the love that had shaped who I was,” Chan says. “When I received the news that she had taken her own life, everything I had buried came back at once. I cried like a child. My heart hurt in a way I couldn’t control. And in that moment, I understood something very clearly: pain was not what destroyed me. Pain was what proved that love had existed.” He adds that the film does not romanticize suffering. “It asks a quieter, more uncomfortable question: if we remove pain to survive, what parts of ourselves do we also erase?” A Gobelins graduate, Chan recently worked as animation supervisor on “Lost in Starlight,” Netflix’s first Korean animated feature, and has done work for Burberry and Balenciaga. articles.content: Paul Howard, son of The Three Stooges ‘ Moe Howard, died earlier this week in Manhattan. He was 91. Paul Howard remained a guardian of his father’s legacy throughout his life, meeting generations of Stooges fans at conventions and events where he shared personal stories, family memories and insights into the life of Moe Howard. In 2015, Paul Howard hosted the docuseries “Hey Moe, Hey Dad!,” which related the legacy of The Three Stooges over nine episodes featuring archival footage, family accounts and interviews with family members of Moe Howard, Larry Fine, Curly Howard, Shemp Howard and Curly Joe DeRita. articles.title: David Del Valle, Admired Historian of Horror Films, Dies at 77
articles.summary: He provided commentary for many home video releases and conducted what many consider to be the quintessential Vincent Price interview.
articles.content: David Del Valle, the encyclopedic horror film historian, author and raconteur who contributed to dozens of laserdisc, DVD and Blu-ray commentary tracks during his eclectic career, has died. He was 77. Del Valle died Wednesday at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank after a battle with esophageal cancer, his caregiver and friend, producer Dano Marino, told The Hollywood Reporter . He was living down the street from the apartment on Harold Way in Los Angeles where Dracula star Bela Lugosi died of a heart attack in 1956. “The only way out of Harold Way is apparently feet first,” he joked. His hourlong chat with Price in 1987 is considered the most substantial interview the horror legend ever gave. He also wrote the books Lost Horizons Beneath the Hollywood Sign and Six Reels Under , published in 2010 and 2012, respectively, and articles for Fangoria magazine; penned an online column called “Camp David” for Films in Review ; and introduced a weekly screening of horror films in 2020 for the channel/app Full Moon Features. articles.summary: The award-winning short film, directed by Teboho Edkins and produced by his father, dives into the mourning following the death of the filmmaker’s brother in a Boeing airplane crash over Ethiopia.
articles.content: In March 2019, a Boeing 737 MAX crashed in Ethiopia just six minutes after taking off from the airport in the country’s capital, Addis Ababa. It had 157 people on board, and all of them died. Among them was Max Thabiso Edkins . His older brother Teboho Edkins decided to make a film about the experience of grief and mourning that his family and the local community went through. The result is the very personal 38-minute short film an open field , directed by Edkins and produced by his father, Don Edkins, and Carine Chichkowsky. The film is now going global, hitting Netflix on Dec. 1, about a year after its world premiere at the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam ( IDFA ) 2025, where it won the best short documentary award. In an open field, the filmmaker finds out that dozens of nearby villagers immediately converged on the crash site to help. Some even stood vigil for a month to protect and preserve the area. articles.content: The year’s second adaptation of an ancient, magic epic is a welcome, wonderful contrast to Christopher Nolan’s grim, harrowing “The Odyssey” In case you haven’t noticed, it’s been an atypically good year for big budget film adaptations of 3,000-year-old fantasy epics. At least, I think it’s atypical. If last year’s “Zootopia 2” and “F1: The Movie” were stealth reboots of “The Epic of Gilgamesh” and “Beowulf,” they hid it really, really well. Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” was the talk of the town this summer, with an all-star cast and an exceptionally dour take on Homer’s classic saga. Lots of greys, lots of misery, lots of monsters. People like that kind of thing nowadays. It’s a great movie but if you thought it was a bit of a downer, Nitesh Tiwari’s “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend” is the three-hour magical action spectacle for you. It’s an electric rainbow of a movie, shimmering with extravagance, and brimming with more adventure and romance than a movie theater can usually handle. American audiences are probably less familiar with Valmiki’s Hindu poem “Ramayana” than they are with “The Odyssey,” in part because a lot of teenagers in this country are required to read Homer in high school, and in part because “The Odyssey” is constantly referenced throughout Western popular culture. I’m pretty sure there’s never been a screwball bluegrass musical version of the “Ramayana” but then again, I’m one of those Americans who wasn’t exposed to Valmiki’s epic in school, so I could be wrong. articles.title: Sebastián Lelio, Chilean Director of Oscar-Winning ‘A Fantastic Woman,’ Dead at 52
articles.summary: Lelio, who was found dead at his home in Santiago amid a health issue, also directed "Gloria" star Paulina García to a Silver Bear win in 2013 before remaking the film as "Gloria Bell" with Julianne Moore in 2018.
articles.content: Sebastián Lelio, the humanistic Chilean filmmaker whose trans drama “A Fantastic Woman” won the Best International Feature Film Oscar in 2018, has died at age 52. The Chilean publication Emol first revealed the news that he was found dead in his home in Santiago on Friday, November 6, amid an undisclosed health issue. His body was discovered by his partner, the actress/director Amalia Kassai, who starred in his final film, the protest musical “The Wave” from Cannes 2025. Kassai also posted a statement in Spanish on her Instagram account . “It’s with much sadness that we share the passing due to health problems of the Chilean filmmaker Sebastián Lelio,” her statement read, as translated independently by IndieWire. “We are going through a moment of much pain, and his memory will always remain with us. He was a beautiful person and shared the Chilean culture in huge moments in history. The family would like to ask for privacy and consideration in these difficult moments.” Related Stories Emily Feingold Hired as EVP, Communications for The Walt Disney Company James Gray on His ‘Only Real Beef with Streaming’ and the ‘Recurring Nightmare’ That Started at Cannes in 2009 Lelio was reportedly mid-production on the feature “Chilean Poet,” adapted from Alejandro Zambra’s Viking-published 2022 novel. Along with “A Fantastic Woman,” he also directed the Hasidic lesbian romance “Disobedience” in the same year, 2017; it starred Rachel McAdams and Rachel Weisz, and helped bring the filmmaker to international prominence. In 2013, he directed Paulina García to a Berlinale Silver Bear Best Actress win with “Gloria,” a late-in-life romantic comedy about a 58-year-old divorcee starting over again. He remade his own film in 2018 in English as “Gloria Bell,” released by A24 and starring Julianne Moore in the role García originated, opposite John Turturro. articles.title: Emily Feingold Hired as EVP, Communications for The Walt Disney Company
articles.summary: The former Netflix communications guru will join Disney as David Jefferson departs.
articles.content: Emily Feingold has been named Executive Vice President, Communications for The Walt Disney Company . She will begin her job next Monday. Feingold is a veteran executive and is widely respected by the press as a straight shooter. She joins Disney after nearly nine years at Netflix , where she rose to become Vice President and Head of Communications for the U.S. and Canada. At the streaming giant, Feingold worked on corporate, financial, product and technology, advertising, content, marketing and consumer products communications. She advised senior leadership through some of Netflix’s biggest moments, including when co-founder Reed Hastings was succeeded as CEO by Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters. She also was in place when Netflix moved into advertising, live events, and gaming, as well as during its failed bid for Warner Bros. Discovery. articles.summary: Gray joined IndieWire's "Screen Talk" podcast live at the Virginia Film Festival to talk "Paper Tiger," "Little Odessa," and more in an amusingly wide-ranging chat.
articles.content: James Gray time-travels back to his Queens roots once again for his latest film , “ Paper Tiger .” It’s a location, an atmosphere, a state of mind he’s explored across decades and genres, dating back to his 1994 debut feature, “ Little Odessa .” Like “Paper Tiger,” “Little Odessa” also featured the shadows of the Russian mafia looming over a family unit — to devastating ends. But even 30-plus years later, with his new movie — starring Miles Teller, Adam Driver, and Scarlett Johansson — Gray wanted to go just as dangerous. Adam Driver, for one, has danger in him, according to Gray, who cast the Oscar nominee as a former police officer who links up with the red mafia in the 1980s.
